sections.title: What You Are Learning
paragraphs: AWS provides purpose-built database services because not every database problem is the same. The exam asks you to identify the database type, management model, and migration tool that match the workload.
sections.callout: What kind of database does the workload need?

sections.title: Maestro Mental Model
sections.callout: CONTROL · RELATIONAL · NOSQL · CACHE · MOVE · CONVERT

sections.title: EC2-Hosted vs. AWS-Managed Databases

entries.title: Database on Amazon EC2
paragraphs: The customer installs and operates database software on a virtual server, gaining more control while accepting responsibility for tasks such as operating-system management, database installation, configuration, patching, and maintenance.

entries.title: AWS-Managed Database
paragraphs: AWS handles more infrastructure and routine operational work, depending on the service, so customers can focus more on applications and data.

sections.callout: Managed does not mean the customer has no responsibility.

sections.title: Relational Databases
paragraphs: Relational databases organize structured data in tables and use schemas and relationships to represent the data model.

entries.title: Amazon RDS
paragraphs: Amazon Relational Database Service makes it easier to set up, operate, and scale supported relational database engines.

entries.title: Amazon Aurora
paragraphs: Amazon Aurora is an AWS-designed managed relational database engine compatible with MySQL and PostgreSQL.

table.caption: Separate the managed service from the AWS-designed engine
rows: Managed service supporting relational database engines
AWS-designed relational engine compatible with MySQL and PostgreSQL

sections.title: NoSQL and Amazon DynamoDB
paragraphs: NoSQL databases use non-relational models such as key-value or document structures. Amazon DynamoDB is a fully managed serverless NoSQL database that supports key-value and document data models.
sections.callout: Managed key-value or document database → Amazon DynamoDB

sections.title: Amazon ElastiCache
paragraphs: Amazon ElastiCache provides managed in-memory caching. Keeping frequently accessed information in memory can improve application response times and reduce repeated load on backend databases.
sections.callout: In-memory cache or frequently accessed data → Amazon ElastiCache

table.caption: Match the data need to the service category
rows: AWS relational engine compatible with MySQL/PostgreSQL
Managed NoSQL key-value or document database

sections.title: Database Migration
paragraphs: Database migration moves data from a source database to a target environment and may also require schema conversion when the source and destination engines differ.

entries.title: AWS Database Migration Service
paragraphs: AWS DMS migrates and replicates database data between supported sources and targets and can help limit downtime by allowing the source to remain operational during migration.

entries.title: AWS Schema Conversion Tool
paragraphs: AWS SCT assesses and converts schemas and code objects when the source and target database engines use different structures.

sections.title: Migration Sequence
paragraphs: When database engines differ, AWS SCT can convert the required schema components and AWS DMS can then migrate or replicate the data. The two tools may be used together.
sections.callout: Convert with SCT, then move with DMS.

sections.title: GSA Scenario Recognition
bullets: Complete OS and database control → Database on EC2
AWS manages more database infrastructure → Managed database service
AWS relational engine compatible with MySQL/PostgreSQL → Aurora
NoSQL key-value or document database → DynamoDB
Migrate or replicate database data → DMS
sections.callout: Find the database model or migration action.

entries.title: EC2 Database vs. Managed Database
paragraphs: Database on EC2 → more control and customer management. Managed database → AWS handles more routine infrastructure work.

entries.title: RDS vs. Aurora
paragraphs: RDS is the managed relational service. Aurora is an AWS-designed relational engine compatible with MySQL and PostgreSQL.

entries.title: RDS vs. DynamoDB
paragraphs: Relational tables and schemas → RDS or Aurora. Key-value or document NoSQL → DynamoDB.

entries.title: DynamoDB vs. ElastiCache
paragraphs: Persistent NoSQL data → DynamoDB. In-memory cache for frequently accessed data → ElastiCache.

entries.title: DMS vs. SCT
paragraphs: Move or replicate data → DMS. Convert schemas and code objects → SCT.

sections.title: Maestro Recognition Sheet
sections.callout: EC2 = CONTROL · RDS = RELATIONAL · DYNAMODB = NOSQL · DMS = MOVE · SCT = CONVERT
